title: Understanding the Relationship between Prompts and Response Uncertainty in Large Language Models
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are widely used in decision-making, but their reliability, especially in critical tasks like healthcare, is not well-established. Therefore, understanding how LLMs reason and make decisions is crucial for their safe deployment. This paper investigates how the uncertainty of responses generated by LLMs relates to the information provided in the input prompt. Leveraging the insight that LLMs learn to infer latent concepts during pretraining, we propose a prompt-response concept model that explains how LLMs generate responses and helps understand the relationship between prompts and response uncertainty. We show that the uncertainty decreases as the prompt's informativeness increases, similar to epistemic uncertainty. Our detailed experimental results on real-world datasets validate our proposed model.

claims.text: LLM response uncertainty decreases as prompt informativeness increases.
Reducible response uncertainty in LLMs corresponds to epistemic uncertainty in latent concepts.
LLM response uncertainty decreases as model quality increases.
Prompt token corruption monotonically decreases multiple-choice response accuracy across tested LLMs.
Prompt token corruption increases empirical response conditional entropy across tested LLMs.
Prompts containing multiple concepts or sub-tasks produce higher response uncertainty than single-concept prompts of equal token length.
Inserting semantically meaningful but task-irrelevant sentences into a prompt increases response uncertainty.

limitations.text: The PRC model assumes an idealized version of LLMs that perfectly learn concept mapping functions, whereas real LLMs deviate when encountering exemplar ordering sensitivity or adversarial inputs.
The proposed framework does not capture sensitivity to the order of exemplars in in-context learning.
The paper does not evaluate the appropriateness of substituting human subjects with LLMs in behavioral simulations.
Controlling response variability solely by adjusting decoding hyperparameters like temperature can be detrimental to tasks requiring reproducibility or obscure user preferences.

future_work.text: Refining the Prompt-Response Concept (PRC) model to incorporate adversarial behaviors and real-world LLM imperfections.
Exploring the application of the PRC model in additional high-stakes decision-making domains requiring reliable LLM responses.

methodologies.name: Prompt-Response Concept (PRC) Model
methodologies.description: A theoretical model representing LLMs as compositions of prompt-to-prompt-concept, concept-to-concept, and concept-to-response mapping functions to quantify prompt informativeness and response entropy.
conditions: Fixed LLM hyperparameters (e.g. fixed temperature T=1)
